blind_implementation: независимый агент (workflow wf_1ffcb6f5-2c9): входы FEATURE_SPEC + data.js/evidence.js + сценарии без ожидаемых значений; аудит доступа: файлы K09 не открывались
note: слепая реализация строилась на 17 исходных случаях (до добавления 8 новых случаев W8); новые случаи W8 ею не проверялись
blind_spec_ambiguities: The spec does not say how to finish the haversine calculation. I used 2*R*asin(sqrt(h)) with math.radians, clamping h to [0,1]. The equivalent atan2 form with deg*pi/180 differs by at most 4.5e-13 m in every ok case. So an unrounded comparison against another implementation needs a tolerance of about 1e-9 m, not bit-for-bit equality.

'Stable choice by ID' does not name the ordering. I used plain code-point string order and picked the smallest ID. Ties only happen where records have identical coordinates: W2 cp1 (baeda67d < bcd265d0, distance 0), W4 cp1 (four clinics at 69.5958,42.3167, so 059c59dd wins), and W4 cp2 (50802484 / 622b4786 / e1b19ead, so 50802484 wins). The IDs of another implementation can only differ in these three rows.

The spec does not cover a tie where the proposed object is exactly as far as the nearest existing record. after=min(before,d_prop) is the same either way. For nearest_after_id I take the smallest ID among the tied records. Another reading keeps the existing record whenever there is no strict improvement. No case contains such a tie, and every UUID here sorts before 'proj1', so both readings give the same result.

With no project, or when the project is farther away, I set after equal to before (the same float), so delta=0.0 exactly and nearest_after_id equals nearest_before_id. The case of no candidates (before=null, after=d_prop, delta=null) is implemented but no case reaches it.

Bbox containment is treated as inclusive on all edges, both for selecting candidates and for rejecting points. No point lies on an edge. All school and outpatient_clinic places in data.js are inside their city bbox, so the bbox filter removes nothing: candidate counts are Shymkent 15 schools / 16 clinics and Astana 8 schools / 16 clinics.

Candidates are chosen by the place's 'group' field, not its Overture 'category'. So the 'outpatient_clinic' group includes dental_clinic, diagnostics_imaging_or_lab_service, behavioral_or_mental_health_clinic and complementary_and_alternative_medicine, and the 'school' group includes place_of_learning. These are data-semantics caveats that do not change the arithmetic. Duplicate-coordinate QA records are kept, as the spec requires.

The spec does not give the source_snapshot fingerprint algorithm (the values look like 'k09ref-sha256:<64 hex>'). I tried simple sha256 guesses over the canonical candidate JSON, with and without city/category/bbox/R, and the file sha256s; none reproduced the values. My resolution is a format check plus a consistency registry built from the 17 cases: one snapshot per (city, category), and a snapshot that belongs to another slice is rejected. This cannot prove that a snapshot matches the current data, and no case is rejected because of it.

The spec says IDs are 'length-limited' but gives no number. I assumed at most 64 characters and the token charset [A-Za-z0-9_.:-]. ID uniqueness is checked across the control points and the proposed object together.
For 'strict validation' I reject unknown extra fields at top level, in control points and in the proposed object. This is an assumption; no case contains extra fields.
A proposed_object given as an array is rejected as more than one project. An array of length 1 would also be rejected, because the contract says null or an object.

I collect all rejection reasons instead of stopping at the first. For an unknown city the bbox check is skipped because there is no bbox. For an unknown schema_version the remaining fields are still validated; in that case only the version check fails.

The original raw import text of each case was not available, so the strict JSON checks (256 KiB limit, NaN/Infinity/1e999 overflow, duplicate keys) run on the re-serialized scenario. None of the 17 cases contains such values.
